structuralDecisions.decision: Keep distance/lineLength/pointInCircle (src/geometry.ts) package-local inside packages/saturday-playwright-cesium. Do NOT create a new packages/saturday-geo workspace for this feature.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Only one real consumer exists today. I checked saturday-playwright-leaflet/src/fixture.ts (the only other mapping-library package in the monorepo): its distanceBetween() calls turf.distance() against Earth directly and is not radius-parameterized, so it is not a second consumer of this module's radius-parameterized spherical geometry — it solves a different problem. Extracting a shared package now, before a second consumer exists, is exactly the Premature Generalization anti-pattern design-principles.md's Anti-Pattern Radar calls out, and violates Kent Beck's 'fewest elements' once intention-revealing/no-duplication are satisfied. The salvage code's own geometry.ts header already anticipated this and wrote the module with zero 'cesium'/'@playwright/test' imports specifically so the extraction stays cheap later — that design choice is sound and is preserved, only the placement is ratified as package-local now.
tradeOffs: If a second Playwright extension (e.g. a future saturday-playwright-mapbox) needs the same radius-parameterized spherical geometry, it will either duplicate ~60 lines or be the trigger for extracting packages/saturday-geo then — an accepted, explicitly deferred cost, not a decision to silently re-litigate.
Keeps this package's own test suite self-contained (tests/geometry.spec.ts runs under vitest/node with zero cross-package dependency), which is a minor win on top of avoiding the premature split.

fitness.verification: grep/import-boundary check in CI (devops-engineer to wire): fail the build if geometry.ts imports 'cesium' or '@playwright/test'. This is what keeps the extraction cheap if a second consumer ever appears.

tradeOffs: The leaflet package keeps its wider bind surface until a separate order fixes it; this is an accepted, explicitly flagged gap, not a silent omission.

structuralDecisions.decision: CesiumFixture's settle-wait (src/fixture.ts's pollUntilSettled) uses Playwright's own page.waitForFunction(..., { timeout }) rather than a hand-rolled for/while+sleep loop — confirmed compliant with architecture-guardrails.md #5 and ratified as the correct pattern for this package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Read fixture.ts directly: every wait (seam-attached, isSettled) goes through page.waitForFunction with an explicit timeoutMs, and rejects with a message naming the stuck condition (tiles/camera/render/seam) rather than looping with sleep(). Playwright's waitForFunction is the framework-provided bounded-wait primitive here, playing the same role guardrail #5 reserves for CircuitBreaker/ExponentialBackoffStrategy on network calls — there is no network retry in this package, so no CircuitBreaker is needed, but the explicit-timeout requirement is met.

fitness.property: No for/while+sleep polling loop exists in src/fixture.ts; every wait has an explicit timeout
fitness.verification: code review (already satisfied); no automated lint rule distinguishes Playwright's waitForFunction from a custom loop, so this stays a documented judgment call

Residual, accepted risk on the non-WGS84 ellipsoid question: fixture-globe.js's Cesium.Viewer(...) call does not pass an explicit mapProjection, so viewer.scene.mapProjection likely still defaults to Cesium's WGS84 GeographicProjection even though viewer.scene.globe.ellipsoid is Aurelis's 6,000,000m sphere. Every helper in fixture.ts reads viewer.scene.globe.ellipsoid directly (never scene.mapProjection), and the fixture never switches to 2D/Columbus view (sceneModePicker: false), so this mismatch is inert for every acceptance criterion this suite exercises. This is a judgment-only call, not independently verifiable by a fitness function without exercising Cesium's internal 2D/Columbus code paths — flag it in the delivery record rather than silently closing the analyst's open question.
openQuestions: If a second Playwright-extension package ever needs radius-parameterized spherical geometry, that is the trigger to extract packages/saturday-geo — not a decision to make speculatively now. No action needed unless/until that second consumer appears.
